title: Merchandise Purchases — Calculation Sheet for the Shelf-Price Correction Amount
content:
Refund Accounting works out the amount of a Price Accuracy Promise correction on a Merchandise Purchases unit as follows.

## Definitions

(a) **Shelf overcharge** — the unit's selling price less its shelf ticket price.

(b) **Sales tax on the shelf overcharge** — the unit's tax amount times the shelf overcharge divided by the unit's selling price, rounded half up to the cent.

(c) **Standing days** — the calendar days from the purchase date to the request date, not counting the purchase date, rounded down to a whole number of weeks and multiplied by seven.

(d) **Standing accrual** — the per-day standing accrual of $0.50 times the standing days.

(e) **Accuracy share** — 20 percent. **Accuracy spend bonus** — $0.00. **Accuracy credit cap** — $15.00.

(f) **Price-accuracy credit** — the accuracy share of the shelf overcharge plus the standing accrual plus the accuracy spend bonus. The price-accuracy credit never exceeds the accuracy credit cap; the cap is compared with that sum after all three parts are added and before the credit is joined to the shelf overcharge and its tax.

(g) **Correction amount** — the shelf overcharge plus the sales tax on the shelf overcharge plus the capped price-accuracy credit, rounded half up to the cent.

## Worked sheet A (hypothetical figures)

Selling price $60.00, shelf ticket price $50.00, tax amount $4.80; purchase date 1 March, request date 20 March.

| Line | Working | Figure |
|---|---|---|
| Shelf overcharge | $60.00 less $50.00 | $10.00 |
| Tax on it | $4.80 times $10.00 divided by $60.00 | $0.80 |
| Standing days | 19 days after the purchase date, rounded down to 2 whole weeks, times seven | 14 |
| Standing accrual | $0.50 times 14 | $7.00 |
| Credit before the cap | 20 percent of $10.00, plus $7.00, plus $0.00 | $9.00 |
| Capped credit | $9.00 is below $15.00 | $9.00 |
| Correction amount | $10.00 plus $0.80 plus $9.00 | $19.80 |

## Worked sheet B — the cap reached (hypothetical figures)

Selling price $240.00, shelf ticket price $200.00, tax amount $19.20; 35 days after the purchase date (exactly 5 weeks, so 35 standing days).

- Shelf overcharge $40.00; tax on it $19.20 times $40.00 divided by $240.00, $3.20.
- Credit before the cap: 20 percent of $40.00 ($8.00) plus $0.50 times 35 ($17.50) plus $0.00, that is $25.50; capped at $15.00.
- Correction amount: $40.00 plus $3.20 plus $15.00, that is $58.20.

## Points of reading

- The cap applies to the price-accuracy credit alone; the shelf overcharge and its tax are never reduced by it.
- Standing days of 6 after the purchase date round down to 0 whole weeks, giving no standing accrual.
